ELI5: Why does a gallon of milk cost more than a gallon of gasoline?

Reasons sorted in order from least relevant to most relevant:

  • Milk squirts out the bottom of an animal that needs to be raised and fed. Mostly irrelevant because drilling and refining oil isn't easy either
  • You pay for packaging when you buy milk.
  • Milk is price controlled in many places. In other words they pour milk out to create an artificial shortage so they can guarantee sale prices to farmers.
  • And winner of most relevant reason: Milk is perishable. The entire time it exists someone has to pay for refrigeration of the stuff, and if nobody buys it it goes to waste forcing both farmers and middle men to raise prices to recoup losses from spoiled product

Not in the same way. You leave a can of gas in your garage for six months and it may make your engine run a bit crappy. You leave milk unrefrigerated for 12 hours, and you might as well throw it away.

The costs and processes associated with producing these two items is vastly different in many ways, but the basic differences between the two that probably accounts for most of the cost difference is the scale of production and automation.

Oil production and refining happens on a massive scale (I'm not sure what the figure is in terms of barrels per day but it's huge), with the majority of the process happening without human intervention. Human hands touching any process is what makes a thing cost a lot more.

Meanwhile on a dairy farm you're talking about squeezing a gallon or so at a time from a large animal that needs to be fed and watered and cleaned up after a great deal. Even if the milking process itself might be automated, there are still a lot of people involved in the process from start to finish, and those people need to be paid. Even in giant dairy farms, the amount of product produced pales in comparison to oil refinery output.

So smaller production and more hands on the product along the way make milk more expensive than gas.

Milk is goes bad after a short time (a few weeks). So we can't buy milk too far from where it was collected from the cow, or else it will take too long to get it to the supermarket and be sold. We also have to put it in special containers to prevent it from germs getting in it, which is why your mother always says "Don't drink from the carton!", because germs from your mouth spill into the milk and make it go bad after a few days.

Crude Oil has been sitting around for millions of years, so it won't go bad. That means Crude Oil can be purchased from anywhere in the world at the best deal. Crude oil is very dirty, so we can transport it in dirty containers.Transporting it in giant, dirty, containers is cheap.

From Crude Oil, we can make gasoline. Gasoline needs to be clean, but not germ free, so it's still easier than transporting milk. It's transported on huge container trucks, which is way cheaper than a milk truck full of cartons and jugs.

Then, when you put it in the car, it's just a hose connected to a big underground tank. No packaging or anything.

So being able to move liquid in tanker ships and tanker trucks is cheaper than packaging it and moving it in container trucks.
Considering you don't drive to the milk dispenser with your own tank and pump out a gallon, i'd say the difference isn't that bad.

One of my favorite documentaries about survival against all odds. The plot:

In the mid-80's two young climbers attempted to reach the summit of Siula Grande in Peru; a feat that had previously been attempted but never achieved. With an extra man looking after base camp, Simon and Joe set off to scale the mount in one long push over several days. The peak is reached, however on the descent Joe falls and breaks his leg. Despite what it means, the two continue with Simon letting Joe out on a rope for 300 meters, then descending to join him and so on. However when Joe goes out over an overhang with no way of climbing back up, Simon makes the decision to cut the rope. Joe falls into a crevasse and Simon, assuming him dead, continues back down. Joe however survives the fall and was lucky to hit a ledge in the crevasse. 

This is the story of how he got back down
